stories.title: 60 hours of improvisation: Michigan musicians set a record for the world's longest jam
stories.summary: It was hours and hours of music — 60 hours in all — of "record breaking" music. Musicians in Michigan played and improvised in what they believe is now the world's longest jam.

stories.title: New revelations in Cornell sexual assault case spark outrage
stories.summary: The alleged victim of a 2024 gang rape at Cornell University clearly said in her police statement that she was sexually assaulted, her attorney told NPR — counter to what a prosecutor has claimed.

stories.title: The White Sox say their fan in the Vatican may be the extra boost they needed
stories.summary: The Chicago White Sox won their first playoff series since 2005. The victory feels more sacred now that the team has revealed Pope Leo's letter invoking "Almighty abundant  blessing" toward the team.

stories.title: Failed execution attempts are not uncommon in the U.S.
stories.summary: The failed execution attempt of a woman in Tennessee on Wednesday wasn't the first time this has happened. The state's execution protocols have been under scrutiny for years.

stories.title: This week in science: Loud birds, eating with company, and asteroid samples
stories.summary: NPR's Short Wave podcast talks about really loud birds, the benefits of eating with company and what asteroid samples could tell us about the early Earth.

stories.title: Former federal regulator says existing laws already apply to AI
stories.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Lina Khan, chair of the Federal Trade Commission in the Biden administration, about her op-ed "There Are Plenty of Laws on the Books to Check the A.I. Giants. Use Them."
